record.paper_title: Open problems concerning the Hőlder continuity of the direction of vorticity for the Navier-Stokes equations.
record.context_brief: Navier-Stokes velocity integrability from vorticity-direction Hölder regularity
record.original_question: Let u be a Leray-Hopf weak solution of the three-dimensional evolution Navier-Stokes equations in the whole space R^3 on the time interval (0,T), and let its vorticity be ω = ∇×u. For θ(x,y,t) equal to the angle between ω(x,t) and ω(y,t), assume the direction of vorticity is β-Hölder in the sense that sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x-y|^β on R^3×R^3×(0,T) for some β < 1/2. Must u have additional space-time integrability: do there exist exponents s and q such that u belongs to L^s(0,T; L^q(R^3)) and λ(s,q) = 2/s + 3/q < 3/2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $u$ be a Leray–Hopf weak solution of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations
\[
\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u - \Delta u + \nabla p = 0,\qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0,
\]
on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times (0,T)$, and let its vorticity be $\omega = \nabla\times u$. For points $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^3$ and $t\in(0,T)$, let $\theta(x,y,t)$ denote the angle between the vectors $\omega(x,t)$ and $\omega(y,t)$. Assume that the direction of vorticity is $\beta$-Hölder continuous in space in the sense that there exist constants $c>0$ and $\beta\in(0,1/2)$ such that
\[
\sin\theta(x,y,t) \le c\,|x-y|^{\beta} \qquad \text{for all } (x,y,t)\in\mathbb{R}^3\times\mathbb{R}^3\times(0,T).
\]
For exponents $s,q\in[1,\infty]$, set $\lambda(s,q) = \tfrac{2}{s} + \tfrac{3}{q}$.

Question: Under the above hypothesis with some $\beta<1/2$, must there exist exponents $s$ and $q$ such that
\[
u \in L^s\bigl(0,T;\,L^q(\mathbb{R}^3)\bigr) \qquad \text{and} \qquad \lambda(s,q) = \tfrac{2}{s} + \tfrac{3}{q} < \tfrac{3}{2}\,?
\]
artifact.status_search_result: The strongest known result handles the borderline case β = 1/2 (Berselli–Beirão da Veiga, 2002), giving ω ∈ L^∞(L²) and hence smoothness. Extending the regularity/integrability conclusion to β < 1/2 is explicitly identified as an open problem in subsequent surveys and follow-up papers, with no full solution reported as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Navier-Stokes equations: Some questions related to the direction of the vorticity
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses open questions related to Hölder continuity exponents of the direction of vorticity and induced integrability of u.
status_evidence.claim: The case β<1/2 remains an open problem in the regularity theory via direction-of-vorticity hypotheses.

status_evidence.title: Direction of Vorticity and a Refined Regularity Criterion for the Navier–Stokes Equations with Fractional Laplacian
status_evidence.snippet: Refines regularity criteria based on direction of vorticity, citing β=1/2 as the up-to-date strongest threshold.
status_evidence.claim: β=1/2 is the threshold currently reached; sub-1/2 Hölder exponents remain unresolved.
